fields.v: Ding, F. (2026). What the Specification Did Not Say: Specification–Oracle Gaps in Test-Graded Coding-Agent Benchmarks. arXiv:2610.30635v1 [cs.CL], 22 Oct 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2610.30635v1 [cs.CL]; no published venue stated
Alibaba Group (single author, Fei Ding)

Evaluates; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — defines specification–oracle gaps (tests that depend on names, paths or literals the natural-language task specification does not state), builds a static audit for five languages, and evaluates SWE-Milestone v1.0.2 (98 graded milestones, 35 published agent runs) in depth plus four further benchmarks (SWE-EVO, SWE-Chain, SWE-bench Verified, DeepSWE) from public data; no agents run by the author
fields.why: Main vs secondary order is a judgement: the contributions list (p. 1-2) puts the definition/taxonomy and the static audit (an evaluation method for test-graded benchmarks, validated in RQ4) first, and the SWE-Milestone study second; the paper runs no agents and re-analyses published runs. 'Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Evaluates' fits as well as the current order.
fields.doubt: O artigo propõe uma auditoria (método de avaliação de benchmarks) e aplica-a ao SWE-Milestone sem correr agentes. Decide se a natureza principal é Evaluates ou Proposes an evaluation method.

fields.v: No SDD approach. Object of study: benchmark task specifications (SWE-Milestone LLM-generated software requirements specifications, SRS; release notes in SWE-EVO; LLM summaries in SWE-Chain; screened issues in SWE-bench Verified; instructions written for the tests in DeepSWE). Published runs of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenHands with 27 models (versions Not stated)

None prescribed for development. Benchmark artefacts studied: per-milestone SRS generated by an LLM pipeline from the milestone's commits, reference (gold) tests as oracle, filter lists. Proposed: corrected filter lists (3,321 conservative / 3,964 full entries) and specification addenda for the 25 affected milestones stating 153 interface conventions the tests rely on (e.g. 'the package rest/handler must declare valueSSE')

Not stated for agents. SWE-Milestone end-to-end mode: agent starts from a trial base and implements all milestones in one working tree, choosing the order among milestones whose prerequisites are done; grading copies gold tests onto the agent's code per milestone

None in the agent runs studied. Audit validation: held-out cases labelled blind by a hired software expert and by the author; LLM-drafted first-pass verdicts checked by the author for other benchmarks

N/A (no SDD approach); not run, document-based: static analysis of benchmark task specifications (SRS, release notes, issues, instructions) against their test oracles, using published run results; no agent runs by the author
fields.why: No SDD approach is evaluated and the author runs no agents (Ethics statement, p. 9); what is analysed is benchmark task specifications (SRS, release notes, issues, instructions) against their test oracles. N/A (as for other records without an SDD approach) and 'not run, document-based' both fit; 'specification format only' would treat benchmark task texts as an SDD artefact.
fields.doubt: O estudo não aplica nenhuma abordagem SDD nem corre agentes; analisa especificações de tarefas de benchmarks contra os testes. Decide entre N/A (sem abordagem SDD) e 'not run, document-based'.

fields.v: Not classifiable (benchmark task specifications; authors' wording 'software requirements specification (SRS)', 'specification–oracle gap', 'specification addenda')
Existing code bases: long-horizon milestone evolution of real repositories from a trial base (SWE-Milestone); issue and release-level tasks in the other benchmarks

SWE-Milestone v1.0.2: 7 repositories, 98 graded milestones, 580,039 required tests, 35 published end-to-end runs (28 on the leaderboard) over 27 models; other benchmarks: SWE-EVO 48 tasks, SWE-Chain 155 steps, SWE-bench Verified 500 instances (78 submissions >= 60% resolved), DeepSWE 113 tasks (280 trials on the flagged task). Validation: 111 development cases, held-out 94 + 103 cases
Open-source repositories: go-zero (Go), navidrome (Go+TS), nushell and ripgrep (Rust), scikit-learn (Python), element-web (TypeScript), dubbo (Java)
N/A (no participants). Validation labeller: hired software expert with over ten years of full-stack and open-source maintenance experience; plus the author
None for agents. Audit cost: 28.1 minutes on a 16-core workstation, at most 1,333 MiB memory, no model calls

Benchmark metrics re-computed: per-milestone recall (share of required new tests passed), precision ((f+1)/(f+b+1)), score (F1), resolve rate (all required tests pass); unit failure rate per (unit, run)
None
None

Prevalence of hidden dependencies (milestones and tests at risk); failure lift (rate ratio) and odds ratio of blocked vs comparable units; Kendall tau-b between original and re-scored rankings; audit precision and recall (Wilson intervals); inter-rater Cohen's kappa; rate at which runs reproduce hidden names; agreement between runs (Cohen's kappa); cutoff-exposure correlation

Automatic: static extractors per language (Go go/ast, Python ast, tree-sitter for TypeScript, Rust, Java) and a language-independent core diffing gold states; re-scoring with the harness's own scoring code (matches leaderboard within 0.20 points); counterfactual rebuilds renaming one hidden name (Go); bootstrap over milestones, logistic regression with two-way cluster-robust errors, random-removal baseline, permutation test. Manual: blind labelling of held-out cases by a hired expert and the author (kappa 0.92 and 0.96); log reading; LLM-drafted verdicts checked by the author for other benchmarks

N/A (no configuration run by the author; re-analysis of 35 published SWE-Milestone runs of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenHands with 27 models; per-run values not reported). Aggregate: best published configuration resolve rate 29.75% over 98 milestones; re-scoring without gap-affected tests (full variant) raises the 28 leaderboard runs by +0.84 score points on average (-0.26 to +2.89) and +0.47 resolve points (max +2.78); go-zero mean score 38.33 -> 42.08, resolve 4.35% -> 5.71%

Comparison of units, not of SDD configurations: (unit, run) pairs of units blocked by a hard hidden dependency vs units within the same milestones that carry new tests without new dependencies; logistic regression with unit size and repository fixed effects, clustered by milestone and model family; re-scored vs published rankings (Kendall tau-b) against random removals of matched size; counterfactual on the reference (Go, 128 cases). Agent, model and repetitions as in the published runs (not controlled by the author). Cross-benchmark comparison exploratory (different review units and sizes)

25 of 98 milestones have a hard hidden dependency (0.6% of required tests at risk; go-zero 15/23 milestones, 7.1% of tests). Blocked units fail in 80.6% of runs vs 48.4% for comparable units (lift 1.67, 95% CI 1.32-2.04; odds ratio 4.64, CI 2.92-7.37); stated names make no difference (1.08). Renaming one hidden name breaks the unit in 126 of 128 Go cases. Ranking robust (tau-b 0.984 score / 0.942 resolve for 28 runs), within random-removal variation; all 34 neighbouring run pairs have overlapping 95% rank intervals. Other benchmarks: a third or more of tasks affected where specifications are release notes or LLM summaries (SWE-EVO 17/48, SWE-Chain 64/155), almost none where screened or written for tests (Verified 3/500, DeepSWE 7/113 flagged, 1 confirmed); SWE-Chain lift only 1.12 because its harness isolates failed imports and reports them back. Runs reproduce 45% of hard and 79% of inferable hidden names

Audit precision 58/65 (89.2%, Wilson 79.4-94.7%), recall 13/14 (92.9%); reproducible (identical results on repeated runs). Limitations stated: realisation is observational and groups may differ in difficulty; counterfactual covers Go only; some rules set on development data (DeepSWE not out-of-sample); lexical SRS matching; name-level extractors without type checking; behavioural gaps covered only by a heuristic, so counts are a lower bound; cross-benchmark comparison not controlled; addenda not yet tested with agent runs

Limitations as stated in the Limitations section (observational realisation, Go-only counterfactual, rules tuned on development data, lexical matching, name-level extraction, behavioural gaps a lower bound, one benchmark in depth, correlational memorisation analysis, addenda effect not measured). Gaps/recommendations: run a dependency audit when generating specifications and state the names, paths and messages the tests need or exclude tests that reach into internals; replay references in several topological orders; isolate build units and report unresolved names to the agent; publish per-test results. Cause: generator prompts tell the LLM not to over-specify implementation details

Relevant to RQ4: incomplete task specifications (unstated interface names) measurably change agent outcomes, and test-graded evaluations reward reproducing upstream details. Replication: audit, corrected filter lists, addenda and verdicts said to be released; no URL given in the text. Pre-registration: none; rules frozen before drawing the held-out set. Languages: Go, Python, Rust, TypeScript, Java. Inconsistency: single listed author but text refers to 'the authors' and 'one of the authors' labelling cases. One leaked run excluded from name analyses (odds ratio 4.75 without it). LLM coding assistants used for the audit implementation and first-pass verdicts (declared)
